claims.statement: JobRegistry (src-tauri/src/application/jobs.rs) is the host's only job scheduling: one active-job slot and a per-id artifacts map. claim_with_id refuses a second concurrent job with BUSY and an id that already has registered artifacts with JOB_ID_CONFLICT, and on success returns a JobGuard plus the receiving end of a cancel oneshot; every long-running use case (prepare, transcribe, import_transcript, refine_transcript) must claim it first.

JobGuard releases the single slot in Drop by calling JobRegistry::finish, which clears the slot only when the id still matches; because the guard lives inside the async use case, the slot is freed on every exit path — the happy return, an early `?`, a future dropped by cancellation, or an unwinding panic — and callers never release the slot manually or bypass the guard.

The registry's artifacts map is the conceptual repository of finished work: transcription and import register Artifacts under their job id; refinement claims a fresh job id for its own slot but registers the produced minutes under the target transcription's id, so open/reveal keep working from the original result. Lookups for unknown ids or missing minutes fail with ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND, and poisoned registry locks surface as STATE_ERROR rather than a panic.

Cheap, decisive validations run before the job slot is claimed: transcribe validates the speaker hint (INVALID_SPEAKER_HINT, pinned by a test that asserts no workspace access) and refine_transcript resolves the target artifacts and reads the assistant API key (ASSISTANT_KEY_MISSING) before their claim_with_id calls; the engine readiness gate (SETUP_REQUIRED) is the one check that runs inside run_transcription after the claim.

Cancellation crosses the application boundary synchronously: the cancel_job Tauri command forwards to Application::cancel and JobRegistry::cancel, which matches the active id, takes the cancel sender, and sends once on the oneshot without waiting for the worker to die — a wrong id is JOB_NOT_FOUND, a second cancel is ALREADY_CANCELLING, and a send failure because the receiver was already dropped is JOB_FINISHED.

EnginePort::prepare, TranscriptionPort::transcribe, and RefinementPort::refine all take the cancel oneshot receiver and pass it into run_process, which selects on it in two places — inside the stdout/stderr read loop and around the final child.wait() — so cancellation lands whether the worker is chatty or silent; a fake-port test shows cancellation reaching a running job with no timing waits and yielding CANCELLED.

import_transcript claims the job slot but binds the cancel receiver to _unused_cancel: an import is a local file copy with no child process to terminate, and the UI shows no cancel control for it, so a cancel sent during an import can only succeed silently without effect.

When the cancel oneshot fires, run_process first flushes any buffered stderr as one final log event (no log line is lost), then terminate_on_cancel sends SIGTERM to the whole process group, waits at most 3 seconds, sends SIGKILL on timeout, always reaps the child via child.wait (no zombie), disarms the guard, and returns AppError CANCELLED; the awaited use case then returns the error and the JobGuard drop frees the slot immediately.

Children are spawned with a cleared environment, null stdin, kill_on_drop, and their own Unix process group (process_group(0)); ProcessGroupGuard signals -pid so uv-spawned grandchildren die too, and while armed its Drop sends SIGKILL to the group. Normal completion and cancellation disarm it first, so a run_process future dropped mid-flight — protocol error, cancelled task, or panic — cannot leave the worker tree alive.

The webview mints the job id with crypto.randomUUID before invoking the backend (prepare, transcribe, refine), so the very first worker event already belongs to the current job, and reduceJobEvent ignores any event whose jobId differs from the state's — the trailing events of a just-cancelled job cannot leak into a new run.

The frontend job-machine reduces JobViewState through idle/running/completed/failed/cancelled; phase events are dropped once the status is settled (completed/failed/cancelled), and the terminal events completed, prepared, and refined each set status completed at 100% — so the UI settles the moment a cancel is accepted and ignores late phase events from the dying worker.

Within one phase the job-machine's percent only moves forward (Math.max), while entering a new phase adopts that phase's value; log events are split on newlines — undoing the host's stderr batching — prefixed with the stream name, and the buffer keeps only the last 200 lines.

cancelJob records the cancellation as a polite notice with error null, and failJob is a no-op on an already-cancelled state, so the CANCELLED error the backend surfaces as the worker dies never re-reports the user's decision as a failure; on real failures the message slot keeps the stable status line while the cause goes to the alert slot exactly once.

Recording is a second single-slot resource independent of the job slot: Application guards active_recording, start_recording mints a Uuid::now_v7 and fails with RECORDING_BUSY if occupied, stop/cancel verify the id (RECORDING_ID_MISMATCH for a different session, RECORDING_NOT_ACTIVE for an empty slot) and clear the slot regardless of the port call's outcome — a user can record while a transcription runs, but never record twice.

NativeRecorder enforces the same single slot under its own lock; stop finalizes the .wav.part into the meeting folder's final .wav and derives duration_seconds from the frames actually written; cancel stops the writer and removes the partial file (and the folder when left empty); dropping the NativeRecorder also cleans up any still-active recording so app shutdown cannot leave a dangling capture.

The recording-machine mirrors idle/starting/recording/stopping/failed/completed; canStartRecording permits a new start only from idle/completed/failed, and stop, user discard, and native-failure cleanup all converge on the stopping state — which disables the stop and discard buttons — before settling into completed (WAV finalized with its true duration), idle (cancel removes the partial), or failed.

The recording machine measures elapsedSeconds against startedAtMs instead of counting ticks because the webview throttles or suspends interval callbacks in the background; tickRecording recomputes wall-clock elapsed time and clamps a backwards clock to the previous value, RecordingController re-ticks on visibilitychange and focus, and a tick that changed nothing but the clock updates only the time element.

RecordingController parks native failures that arrive while startRecording is still pending and cleans them up once start resolves; for an active recording, cleanupFailure transitions to stopping, cancels the recording to stop the writer and remove the partial file, then surfaces the failure (appending the cleanup failure if even the discard failed); dispose() cancels any active recording when the page unloads.

Cancellation stays exposed while setup, transcription, or refinement runs: each progress card carries its own cancel button (#setup-cancel-button, #cancel-button, #augment-cancel-button) and AppView.setBusy shows exactly the one matching the active busy kind; all three bind to data-action="cancel", which invokes backend.cancel(jobId) and applies cancelJob locally, or reports a polite error when no job id has been minted yet.

Progress reports phase completion, never invented ETAs: the webview's percent and message only mirror the most recent phase event; setup emits fixed stage percentages (5% Python runtime, 22% venv, 35% engine install, 45–50% models, 100% ready), and the worker emits per-phase percentages with refinement reporting completed chunks rather than streamed characters so the bar cannot jump backwards.

Every IPC failure is AppError {code, message} serialized camelCase with a stable ASCII code (BUSY, JOB_ID_CONFLICT, JOB_NOT_FOUND, ALREADY_CANCELLING, JOB_FINISHED, CANCELLED, ARTIFACT_NOT_FOUND, RECORDING_BUSY, RECORDING_ID_MISMATCH, RECORDING_NOT_ACTIVE, STATE_ERROR, SETUP_REQUIRED, INVALID_SPEAKER_HINT, ASSISTANT_KEY_MISSING) and Korean user copy; the frontend errorMessage trusts the message only when the object carries both a string code and a string message, rendering generic unexpected-error copy otherwise while errorDetail preserves the raw diagnostic for the log disclosure.
